original_question: Given a directed acyclic graph G and an integer k >= 0, does there exist a complete sequence of vertex eliminations, where eliminating a vertex j adds all edges from each predecessor of j to each successor of j and costs |P_j| times |S_j|, whose total cost is at most k?
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper’s exact target. It correctly identifies the input as a directed acyclic graph and a budget k, uses vertex eliminations rather than edge eliminations, matches the paper’s vertex-elimination update by connecting every predecessor of j to every successor of j, uses the correct step cost |P_j|·|S_j|, and asks the right decision question: whether there exists a complete elimination sequence of total cost at most k. It also stays with the paper’s purely structural formulation, rather than drifting into the algebraic Jacobian-accumulation setting with edge labels and dependence assumptions.
missing_details: The paper’s formal definition removes the eliminated vertex j from the vertex set: if the current graph is H = (W, F), then eliminating j produces H - j = (W \ {j}, F ∪ {(i, l) : i ∈ P_H(j), l ∈ S_H(j)}).
P_j and S_j should be made explicit as the predecessor and successor sets of j in the current DAG at the moment of elimination, not just in the original graph.
A vertex is eliminatable only if it has both a nonempty predecessor set and a nonempty successor set.
The total cost of a sequence is the sum of the individual vertex-elimination costs.

To be fully stand-alone, the phrase "complete vertex elimination sequence" should be clarified using the nearby context: the paper says complete sequences transform the DAG into a bipartite DAG representing the Jacobian matrix of the underlying numerical program.
The paper phrases k as a "positive integer k ≥ 0"; operationally, this is a nonnegative integer.
The paper’s open problem is specifically the purely structural formulation of vertex elimination; no local derivative labels or algebraic dependence assumptions are part of the input.
refined_question: In the purely structural vertex-elimination formulation arising from Jacobian accumulation, given a directed acyclic graph G = (V, E) and a nonnegative integer k, does there exist a complete vertex-elimination sequence of total cost at most k, where total cost is the sum of step costs, and where at each step in the current DAG H = (W, F) one may eliminate a vertex j only if it has nonempty predecessor and successor sets P_H(j) = {i ∈ W : (i, j) ∈ F} and S_H(j) = {l ∈ W : (j, l) ∈ F}, replacing H by H - j = (W \ {j}, F ∪ {(i, l) : i ∈ P_H(j), l ∈ S_H(j)}) and paying cost |P_H(j)|·|S_H(j)|?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalent stepwise formulation stated in the paper: eliminating a vertex j is the same as front-eliminating all of its in-edges, and equivalently the same as back-eliminating all of its out-edges.
justification: The draft is targeting Open Problem 4.2, not Open Problem 4.1, because it asks about eliminating vertices rather than edges and uses exactly the vertex-elimination cost |P_j|·|S_j| from Definition 4.2. The surrounding Section 4 context supplies the missing formal details: the eliminated vertex is removed, only vertices with nonempty predecessor and successor sets are allowed, complete sequences are the ones considered in the Jacobian-accumulation setting that yield a bipartite DAG, and the problem is the purely structural version. Theorem 4.3 and the paragraph immediately after it explain why this distinction matters: Jacobian Accumulation is NP-complete under algebraic-dependence assumptions, whereas the computational complexity of the purely structural formulations in Definitions 4.1 and 4.2 is stated to be unknown.
